newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - US stocks seen up after jobs data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - US stocks seen up after jobs data.

text.p: U.S. stocks are seen opening higher on Friday after a report on April payrolls, wages and employment, analysts said. The following are their comments:
THOM BROWN, MANAGING DIRECTOR OF RUTHERFORD BROWN AND CATHERWOOD:
-- "It was certainly a positive number as far as the markets are concerned and it's going to have a big impact on the long bond and I'm sure the stock market will tag along with it."

U.S. April payrolls rose 142,000, the Labor Department reported. Wall Street economists had forecast, on average, a rise of 211,000. The unemployment rate stood at 4.9 percent, versus an estimate of 5.2 percent and March's figure of 5.2 percent.
LARRY WACHTEL, ANALYST AT PRUDENTIAL SECURITIES:

-- "Obviously bonds like the non-farm figure though unemployment is disappointing. I don't think this changes the attitude of the Federal Reserve. The decrease in the unemployment rate may trigger the Fed."
-- "The favorable payrolls number is offset by the drop in the unemployment rate. It represents full employment."
HUGH JOHNSON, CHIEF INVESTMENT STRATEGIST AT FIRST ALBANY CORP:

-- "It's hard to find something wrong with the data. It confirms that after a strong first quarter, growth in the second quarter is clearly starting off at a much more moderate pace than the first quarter."

-- There is "very little evidence in these numbers of upward pressure on wages. They mean Fed will put policy on hold for another two months to look at additional employment reports. Although there is tightness in labor markets, as seen in the unemployment rate, the economy has slowed from the very fast first quarter pace."
The 30-year Treasury bond was up 6/32 to yield 6.90 percent shortly after the release of the data.
The S&P 500 future rose 4.05 points to 806.10.
